title: AI Workflows for Private Equity BD Teams, Built on Your Firm's Record
summary: A knowledge graph for private equity connects your firm's deals, decisions, and relationships into one structured foundation. Metal's Context Graph is built for private capital, so every new deal starts with everything your firm has already learned.
body_markdown:
Metal provides out-of-the-box workflows cover Private Equity BD's work from first look to a live deal. Each run reads from the firm's[Context Graph](https://www.metal.ai/blog/understanding-knowledge-graph) and writes its reviewed result back, so the next opportunity starts from a fuller record.


### What Does a Context Layer Change for Private Equity BD Teams?


The work still happens. What changes is what each opportunity is read against.


Metal brings your firm's relationship history, record and judgment into every step: **past conversations with the company, the intermediaries behind each deal, and why the firm passed or moved forward.**

### What Out-of-the-Box Workflows Does Metal Offer Private Equity BD Teams?


Metal ships six out-of-the-box workflows, each built around a question BD has to answer before an opportunity reaches the deal team. The workflows all read from and write back to the same[Context Graph](https://www.metal.ai/blog/understanding-knowledge-graph) .


When a process is unique to the firm, its team builds the workflow in Metal’s Workflow Builder, working alongside Metal to take it into production. The workflow stays the firm’s own. Its team edits the steps, decides who approves each run, and can restore any earlier version.

#### Target Company Sourcing: The Ten Companies Worth a First Call


Target Company Sourcing identifies and scores the top 10 private equity acquisition targets within a defined geography and vertical. Each target is benchmarked against anchor companies the team names, or against PE-standard criteria when there is no anchor, so the shortlist reflects the kind of business the firm already wants to own.


What you get:


-


An overview of the market screened: how many companies were evaluated and how many cleared the bar


-


A scored shortlist, with the top picks and the reasoning behind each score


-


Key themes across the set, such as which business models hold customers longest or how ownership structure tracks with quality


The shortlist is where outreach starts. Any target on it can get a full Initial Company Screening before the first call.


#### Initial Company Screening: Is This a Company Your Firm Would Own?


Initial Company Screening evaluates a private company's suitability for private equity ownership and produces a structured briefing with a recommendation, fit scoring, deep-dive analysis, and internal comparables.


What you get:


-


A verdict with the investment thesis, key risks, a value creation roadmap, and recommended next steps


-


A PE fit score across seven dimensions, from revenue quality and competitive moat to management and value creation potential, with the reasoning behind each score


-


Deep dives on the business, financial profile, market and competitive position, and its management and ownership


-


Comparables from the firm's own record, and a plain statement when there are none rather than a filled gap


Because it reads the firm's own notes alongside the company's materials, a headline figure can sit next to what the team's diligence notes say about it. The briefing frames the first conversation. Whether to pursue stays with the team.


### Banker Tear Sheet: What Each Intermediary Has Actually Brought the Firm


Banker Tear Sheet generates a multi-section tear sheet for an intermediary, whether an investment banker or a broker, covering relationship history, deal track record, third-party PitchBook context, value-add activities, and suggested talking points. It starts from the firm's own CRM activity and deal records, and delivers a formatted *Word* report.


What you get:


-


Every logged meeting and call with the intermediary, who from the firm was there, and when the last touch happened


-


The deal track record: deals introduced, how far each one got, and the sector mix


-


Value-add beyond deals, such as executive introductions and market intelligence, with PitchBook context where it is enabled


-


Suggested talking points for the next touch, plus the gaps in the record and how to close them


Where the record is thin, the tear sheet says so: a deal discussed in a meeting but never logged, or a relationship no one formally owns. Coverage decisions rest on what the firm can actually see.


#### CRM Note Mapper: Every Meeting Lands in the Record


CRM Note Mapper turns meeting notes, written in the team's own shorthand, into structured CRM records. It matches the companies and deals mentioned to existing records, identifies the attendees on both sides, and organizes the content into the fields the CRM expects.


What you get:


-


Notes mapped to the right company, deal, and contacts, as activity notes in DealCloud or Salesforce


-


The firm's own abbreviations and terminology recognized


-


A review screen where every mapped field can be adjusted before anything is written


Nothing reaches the CRM without the team's sign-off. Once it does, the note becomes context for the next conversation with that company.


#### NDA Review: Every NDA Checked Against Your Own Playbook


NDA Review checks each incoming non-disclosure agreement against the firm's own NDA policy, compiled once from its playbook. Anyone on the team can upload or forward an NDA, and it returns every deviation from that policy, sorted by how much it matters.


What you get:


-


Deviations sorted as critical, negotiable, or acceptable, each open to accept, reject, or edit


-


A tracked redline or a clean copy to download in Word


-


Counterparty markups handled as negotiation rounds against the same policy


A person still reviews every NDA before it goes back. What changes is that every reviewer starts from the same playbook.


#### Deal Intake and CIM Review: From Banker Email to Live Deal


Deal Intake and CIM Review turns an inbound teaser or CIM email into a reviewed deal record and an investment scorecard. Forward the email to the firm's intake address, and the workflow identifies the deal and its attachments, extracts the details, and proposes a CRM write-back and document filing for a person to approve. For an eligible CIM, it also researches the sell-side advisor and scores the opportunity.


What you get:


-


A proposed CRM update and document filing, applied only after a person approves it


-


A live deal updated rather than duplicated, with passed and dead deals left alone


-


The sell-side advisor researched and classified, so the team sees who is running the process


-


An investment scorecard for eligible CIMs, built from the CIM's own evidence and the firm's knowledge


The workflow comes ready to run and is fitted to each firm's CRM and file storage, such as DealCloud or Salesforce, so setup means connecting the firm's systems rather than designing the process from scratch. A banker's email becomes a deal the whole firm can see, with the CIM already scored when the deal team opens it.


#### How Accurately Does Metal Read Deal Documents?


In Metal's September 2026 evaluation, the same model and agent answered 51 questions over a real private equity dataset twice: once reading through Metal's context layer, once through a leading enterprise file platform, each via MCP.


-


Metal scored 95.1 out of 100 on quality versus 86.6.


-


On the 17 hardest questions, including EBITDA bridges and conflicting document versions, Metal scored 96.1 versus 83.1.


-


On the structured workflow questions, runs through Metal had 93% fewer tool errors: 1.4 failed tool calls per answer against 18.9.


-


Across all questions, Metal used 41% fewer tokens per answer.
